subject: CareLytic: Clarify LLM training & cross-border transfer controls
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@carelytic.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@carelytic.com
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about data use / no-training request (attached redline)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — CareLytic is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. Before we move forward with a purchase order, our legal/privacy team has a few non-negotiable asks around AI-specific data use:

1) No-training commitment: We require that any customer content sent to Redwood's API be contractually guaranteed not to be used to train or improve models (including fine-tuning and retention for prompt/response ingestion) unless we opt in.
2) Prompt/response ownership: Customer requires explicit ownership/return-of-data language for prompts and model outputs. No license to host or reuse.
3) Subprocessors & transfers: Provide current subprocessor list and confirm whether any subprocessors are outside the EEA/US (we're particularly concerned about transfers to APAC or third countries). If transfers occur, we need SCCs or equivalent safeguards and data flow diagrams.
4) Audit evidence: SOC 2 type II report and confirmation of where logs and KV caches are stored and for how long.

I've attached our redlined DPA for reference (CareLytic_DPA_redline_v1.pdf). Please let me know how Redwood handles these items and whether you can accept our redlines or propose equivalent language.

Appreciate a response today if possible — procurement is on a short timeline.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Sr. Privacy Counsel
CareLytic Health
[Attachment: CareLytic_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@carelytic.com>
Cc: legal@carelytic.com
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions about data use / no-training request (attached redline)

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the redline. Quick note up front: we can and do accommodate no-training commitments for enterprise customers, but the exact contractual language and deployment mode matter (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

High-level answers while I loop in our legal and compliance teams:
- No-training: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can provide a contractual "no model training" commitment and ensure data does not leave the customer's leased capacity. For Redwood-hosted API customers, we offer a dedicated contractual addendum that disallows use of Customer Content for model training or improvement (we call this the "Model Improvement Opt-Out"). We will have legal draft the precise clause.
- Prompt/response ownership: We can accept language that grants you ownership/return rights for Customer Content and model outputs; we'll propose wording that preserves operational telemetry/metrics (aggregated, non-identifying).
- Subprocessors & transfers: Our current subprocessor list is public; I'll include the link and attach it. We support region pinning (US/EU) and execute SCCs where required. If you need data to remain within certain jurisdictions, Dedicated/Private is the most straightforward route.
- Audit evidence: We can provide an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA and detail our log retention and KV cache lifecycles.

I'll loop in Markus (Legal) and Evelyn (Compliance) — they'll propose contractual language and call out any carve-outs. Can we schedule a quick 30-minute call tomorrow to align on redlines? If you prefer, we can send a tracked DocuSign with our proposed edits.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-subprocessors-list.csv (csv)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: CareLytic DPA redline — quick help needed

Team — forwarding CareLytic's redline and note from Emma. Key asks: strict no-training language, explicit ownership of prompts/outputs, subprocessor/transfer confirmation, SOC 2 and KV cache log retention detail. Procurement expects turnaround this week.

Questions:
- Markus: can you draft a short no-training clause compatible with our hosted addendum (and a version for Dedicated/Private)? We should avoid open-ended telemetry carveouts that undermine the commitment.
- Evelyn: can you confirm the exact KV cache retention policy and whether telemetry/metrics are ever stored outside US regions for hosted customers pinned to US?
- Dev: can you prepare a data flow diagram that shows where prompt/response transient state and caches live for both hosted and Dedicated deployments (attach PNG).

Attaching the customer's redline. Thanks all — cc'ing Legal Ops.

[Attachment: CareLytic_DPA_redline_v1.pdf]

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CareLytic DPA redline — quick help needed

Hannah — drafted proposed language below and a short risk note. I kept the clause targeted and included a limited telemetry carveout (aggregated, de-identified metrics) to preserve product stability and safety monitoring.

Proposed clause (for hosted addendum and Dedicated/Private variant):
"Redwood will not use Customer Content (including prompts, responses, or any derivative outputs) to train, fine-tune, or improve any models or model weights, nor will Redwood retain Customer Content for the purpose of model training or improvement, except where explicit written consent is provided by Customer. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may collect and retain aggregated, de-identified operational metrics (e.g., request counts, latency percentiles, error rates) that do not permit reconstruction of Customer Content and are used solely to monitor and maintain service availability and safety."

Risk note: the 'notwithstanding' telemetry carveout should be narrowly scoped and defined in a schedule to prevent ambiguity. For hosted customers, ensure the addendum defines retention windows and the mechanism for opting out. For Dedicated/Private, we can adopt a stronger default position (no training; no telemetry leaving customer VPC unless explicitly permitted).

Attachment: redwood-proposed-no-training-clause.docx

I'll prepare a short redline to CareLytic for review once Dev confirms the data flow diagram and Evelyn confirms retention numbers.

-Markus
Head of Legal
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@carelytic.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, legal@carelytic.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 14:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions about data use / no-training request (attached redline)

Hi Emma — looping back with proposed next steps and language from our Legal team. We've reviewed your redline and can accept a no-training commitment with the draft clause included below. Attached are: our proposed clause (redwood-proposed-no-training-clause.docx) and a data flow diagram for Hosted vs Dedicated (data_flow_diagram.png). We can also provide SOC 2 Type II under an NDA.

Summary of key points we will put into the DPA addendum/Amendment:
- No-training: Redwood will include the clause below in the addendum for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private customers the clause will be enforced by configuration (data residency/single-tenant capacity).
- Ownership: We'll accept language granting Customer ownership of Customer Content and outputs, with a limited carveout for aggregated/de-identified operational metrics.
- Subprocessors & transfers: Current subprocessor list provided; we will execute SCCs for EEA transfers and support region pinning to US-only deployment for CareLytic.
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II report available (we'll share under NDA); KV cache retention for hosted customers is currently 48 hours by default unless a customer selects a shorter TTL; logs retained 90 days for troubleshooting (longer retention available as an add-on).

Proposed legal clause (same as Markus recommended):
"Redwood will not use Customer Content (including prompts, responses, or any derivative outputs) to train, fine-tune, or improve any models or model weights, nor will Redwood retain Customer Content for the purpose of model training or improvement, except where explicit written consent is provided by Customer. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may collect and retain aggregated, de-identified operational metrics (e.g., request counts, latency percentiles, error rates) that do not permit reconstruction of Customer Content and are used solely to monitor and maintain service availability and safety."

Next steps:
1) If that clause is acceptable, I can incorporate it into a tracked DPA/Amendment and send a DocuSign for signature (link below).
2) Dev attached the data flow PNG that shows transient prompt/response states and KV cache lifecycles.
3) Evelyn can answer SOC 2 and retention questions in the follow-up call.

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/containers/ABC-DEF-12345
Attachments: redwood-proposed-no-training-clause.docx, data_flow_diagram.png

Are you free for a 30-minute call Thu 6/12 10:00am PT or Fri 6/13 9:00am PT?

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-proposed-no-training-clause.docx (docx)]
